applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision between the challenger's and defender's chains by treating lack of explicit naming and reliance on inference as decisive, so it does the chain-vs-chain assessment K-C governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side. A link is judged by its support, never by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word; and a verse whose words leave the question open decides nothing by itself.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — read either as barring only individual-verse contrary testing or as also barring explicit-naming/word-for-word requirements; I read it as barring the explicit-naming defect the judge used.
why: The judge calls both chains footed yet finds the link underdetermined because one chain does not explicitly name Joseph and the other rests on an inference, which applies an explicit-statement/word-for-word test rather than weighing chain footing alone.
